risk_reasons: Changes the authorization path of nine Admin API read handlers: after the fold an aal1 admin who reads them today is refused, and a defect here is either an admin control-plane bypass or an admin lockout.

Widens ci:admin-aal2's ROUTES contract to every exported handler under src/app/api/admin/** — this audit is the compensating control ADR 0025 D6 spends so that #1185 can let a bearer through src/proxy.ts branch 4 with the route gate as the ONLY admin check.
Flips the audit's P2 page-parity anchor for six Legacy admin portal pages, including /admin/businesses/[id], whose aal2:false is deliberate and reason-recorded today.
Edits the gate-dependency mock shim in 26 admin route suites; a wrong shim is a silently vacuous authorization test (the #1183 carry-forward).
goal: Every exported handler under src/app/api/admin/** reaches an admin MFA gate that ci:admin-aal2 has vetted — the nine role-only GET handlers end on requireAdminWithAal2 and gain AAL2 plus Admin transport bearer support, and the audit's ROUTES contract proves the property for GET as it already does for the mutation verbs.
non_goals: No src/proxy.ts change: branch 4 still refuses a bearer-only request before the route runs, so a live bearer call stays unprovable on staging until #1185.
No CSRF change and no withSameOriginUnlessBearer — that is #1185. The nine handlers are reads and take no same-origin wrapper.
No CORS or ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS change (#1186 already landed; it is untouched here).
No new gate shape: the allowlist stays at requireAdminWithAal2, requireAdminJson and resolveAdminActor, provenance-checked against CANONICAL.
No ci:admin-contract and no docs/admin-api/ artifacts — that is #1190; this ticket only keeps admin-aal2-audit.ts's gate resolver reusable for it (ADR 0028 D2).
No unification of requireRoleOr401's re-throw onto the gate's internal_error 500 anywhere outside these nine handlers.
No impersonation route behaviour change: /api/admin/impersonation/** already binds credited gates and is only re-scanned by the widened audit.
No page retirement, no nav-config prune, no ADMIN_APP_URL redirect (#1192, #1200-#1203).
No migration, no feature flag, no env var, no new dependency, no production write.
user_visible_behavior: An admin with an aal2 session still reads all nine routes exactly as before — same payloads, same status codes on the success path.

An admin with an aal1 session is refused 403 {error:'mfa_required'} on all nine routes instead of being served. MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED is true on staging and production (#1182), so the Legacy admin portal redirects that admin to /mfa/challenge and the step-up path exists.
A non-admin authenticated caller is refused 403 {error:'Forbidden'}; an unauthenticated caller is refused 401 {error:'Unauthorized'}. Every refusal carries NO_STORE_HEADERS and is never a redirect.
All nine routes accept an Authorization: Bearer aal2 admin token, reachable today only from a non-browser caller because src/proxy.ts branch 4 still refuses it.

5xx behaviour changes on the nine routes: an unexpected non-auth failure inside the gate now returns a clean 500 {error:'internal_error'} instead of requireRoleOr401's re-throw. This is the accepted direction (ADR 0025 D5, ticket 'Watch for'); it is recorded, not unified onto anything else.
GET /api/admin/costs loses its hand-written catch that masked a non-AuthError as 401; the gate replaces both arms.

Six Legacy admin portal pages — /admin/overview, /admin/businesses, /admin/businesses/[id], /admin/costs, /admin/jobs, /admin/notifications — now require an aal2 session and redirect an aal1 admin to /mfa/challenge, because audit rule P2 binds a page to its sibling GET's gate.
ci:admin-aal2 fails a NEW admin route whose GET (or any other exported handler) does not reach a credited gate — previously only POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE were bound.
invariants: Invariant #3 (no unapproved posting) and the admin control plane are unaffected; this ticket only tightens reads.
ci:admin-aal2 keeps its fail-closed posture: an unrecognized gate shape is a FINDING, never a pass, and the allowlist does not grow.
Provenance is unchanged: a credited gate must be bound by an import that RESOLVES to CANONICAL, not merely to a matching basename.
The deny rule (referencesOwnerResolver) stays FILE-scoped and still outranks the allowlist.

Page rule P1 (every admin page carries a gate, pre-auth pages derived from src/proxy.ts) and P2 (read-gate parity with the sibling GET) both keep holding in BOTH directions, with zero allowlist entries.
MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED is never read by the gate or by a route (ADR 0025 D10).
Invariant #12: route handlers orchestrate — the fold replaces auth preamble only and moves no business logic.
Invariant #15: the nine route files stay composition roots importing @/lib/db/server; no domain module gains that import.
Invariant #1: no LLM, external API or long-running work moves into a Next.js route.
admin-aal2-audit.ts's gate resolver stays ONE implementation, exported and reusable, so #1190's ci:admin-contract reuses it rather than forking a second reader (ADR 0028 D2).
edge_cases: The widened ROUTES contract binds every Next.js route export: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS. No admin route exports HEAD or OPTIONS today — CORS preflight is answered in src/proxy.ts (#1186, ADR 0026 D1) and never reaches a handler — so including them costs nothing now and makes a future admin OPTIONS export a deliberate review moment rather than an invisible front door.
scanRouteFile's early-out 'no bound handlers → no findings' still applies, so a route.ts exporting only config (dynamic, runtime) is not a finding.
The deny-rule message and the per-handler finding message say 'mutation handler' today; both must stop saying that, or a GET finding reads as a false statement.

Mixed-verb files: businesses/route.ts and businesses/[id]/route.ts each end BOTH verbs on requireAdminWithAal2 after the fold. The audit already resolves each exported handler independently, so a gated GET must still not clear an ungated sibling — the existing (H3-a)/(H3-a2) pins stay green.

P2 anchor flip: routeGetRequiresAal2 turns true for costs, jobs, notifications, overview, businesses and businesses/[id], so those six pages must pass { aal2: true }. /admin/businesses/[id]'s recorded reason ('Gate parity with GET /api/admin/businesses/[id] — plain admin role, no AAL2') is FALSIFIED by this ticket and its comment must change with the flag; the audit header's worked example at admin-aal2-audit.ts:126-138 must be rewritten to a still-true example or restated, because a false comment in a security audit is worse than none.

P2 is parity, not 'pages need AAL2': /admin/demos, /admin/flagged, /admin/offboardings, /admin/suppressions and /admin/locations/csv-import already pass aal2:true and stay a SUPERSET where their sibling GET is absent or plain — never a finding.

/api/admin/nav-counts has NO sibling page, and it is polled every 60s by the admin sidebar. After the fold an aal1 admin's sidebar poll 403s; with MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED on, that admin never renders an admin page in the first place.

GET /api/admin/businesses/[id]/channels resolves its params and calls asLocationId BEFORE the auth gate today; asLocationId on a malformed id must not leak a different status to an unauthenticated caller, so the gate moves to the FIRST statement of the handler.

GET /api/admin/costs currently returns 401 for ANY non-AuthError from requireRole. After the fold that becomes 500 internal_error; the parse-error 400 and the best-effort margin null-fallback are unchanged.

The 22 suites' verified-identity shim is byte-identical in all 22 (verified by hash); the loadAppUser shim inside the @/lib/db/auth mock is identical too. Four more suites (costs, jobs, nav-counts, businesses/[id]/channels) currently mock requireRole or requireRoleOr401 directly and must move to the same shared shim, or their authorization assertions become vacuous.

vi.mock factories are hoisted above imports, so a shared shim can only be reached from inside a factory via `await import(...)` or through vi.hoisted handles — a plain top-level import of the helper referenced inside the factory is a TDZ error at collection time.

The shared shim must DERIVE transport from the request via the production isBearerRequest (src/lib/auth/admin-transport.ts, Edge-safe with zero imports), never from a caller-set knob: requireAdminWithAal2 reads only authUserId and aal, so a knob-driven 'bearer ok' test would reproduce the cookie test's 200 without ever sending an Authorization header. Each per-route bearer case therefore builds a NextRequest carrying a real Authorization: Bearer header and asserts the seam received it.

src/app/admin/businesses/[id]/__tests__/page-source.test.ts, src/app/admin/__tests__/page-chrome.test.ts and src/__tests__/console-admin-palette.test.ts readFileSync these pages but assert nothing about the aal2 flag; they must stay green without edits.
A page flipped to aal2:true costs one extra Supabase AAL round-trip per server render. That is the same cost the eight already-aal2 admin pages pay.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/app/api/admin/offboardings/route.ts — the canonical folded GET: `const gate = await requireAdminWithAal2(request); if (!gate.ok) return gate.response;` then a try/catch ending in internalError(label, error).

src/app/api/admin/autonomy/suspensions/route.ts and src/app/api/admin/solicitation/breaker/route.ts — a read-only GET deliberately gated with requireAdminWithAal2, with the reason stated in a header comment.
src/app/api/admin/flagged/route.ts — a mixed-verb file where BOTH the GET and the POST end on the gate.
src/lib/auth/admin-mfa-gate.ts internalError + NO_STORE_HEADERS — the admin refusal and fault response shape.

src/app/api/admin/offboardings/__tests__/route.test.ts — the #1183 gate-dependency shim (vi.hoisted handles, @/lib/db/auth loadAppUser, @/lib/auth/mfa, @/lib/auth/verified-identity) that the shared helper extracts verbatim.
scripts/ci/__tests__/admin-aal2-audit.test.ts (H3-a)/(H3-a2) — the mixed-verb fixture style the new GET cases follow.
src/app/admin/offboardings/page.tsx — a page whose requireAdminPage call passes { aal2: true } with the parity reason named in the comment above it.
worker/__tests__/helpers/mock-sql.ts — the repo's precedent for a shared test helper imported from inside a vi.hoisted factory.
test_seams: The nine exported GET handlers, imported directly and called with a hand-built NextRequest.

requireAdminWithAal2 (src/lib/auth/admin-mfa-gate.ts) running for real, with only @/lib/auth/verified-identity, @/lib/auth/mfa and @/lib/db/auth mocked — so a route test exercises the real refusal contract.
The shared gate-dependency shim (src/lib/auth/__tests__/helpers/admin-gate-mocks.ts) — one owner for the identity/AAL/loadAppUser mock triple across 26 suites.
scanRouteFile(path, text) — the pure per-file audit scan, exercised with synthetic fixtures.
routeGetRequiresAal2(text, fromFile) and scanAdminPageFile(path, text, context) — the P2 parity anchor and the page contract.
pnpm ci:admin-aal2 against the real tree — the end-to-end proof that every exported admin handler reaches a credited gate.

rollback_plan: Single PR, no migration and no flag. Revert the merge commit on main and redeploy: the nine GETs return to requireRole/requireRoleOr401, the six pages return to plain admin, and ci:admin-aal2's ROUTES contract narrows back to MUTATION_VERBS. Nothing outside this repo depends on the widened contract yet — #1185 and #1190 are not started. On staging, reset staging to origin/main per deployment-guide.md § Re-sync staging. No data is written, so there is nothing to unwind.
observability: internalError('[admin-mfa-gate] unexpected failure:', err) is the structured console.error that distinguishes a Supabase/DB fault on a folded read from a legitimate 401/403; a spike of it after deploy is the signal that the fold broke a read path.

A 403 {error:'mfa_required'} on an admin GET in Vercel logs is the expected shape for an aal1 admin post-fold; a sustained wall of it means the MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED redirect is not reaching that admin.
ci:admin-aal2's own pass line prints the number of admin route files and pages scanned — a sudden drop means the walk under-collected and the guarantee went vacuous.
